title: Protobuf request parsers must reject bodies that spell one field both snake_case and camelCase
answers: request body has both secret_id and secretId and gets authorized against the wrong secret
protobuf JSON duplicate field alias conflict in MLflow REST request
why does MLflow return 400 when a body contains both snake_case and camelCase keys
gateway secret update authorized on one id but executed on another
body:
Symptom: a user with READ on one gateway secret updates or uses another secret by sending both `secret_id` and `secretId` in one body; the auth check and the handler act on different ids.
Root cause: mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_request_message passed the body to `parse_dict`, which accepts both proto and JSON names and lets the later key win, while basic-auth validators read the raw snake_case key.
Fix pattern: call mlflow/server/handlers.py:_reject_conflicting_field_aliases on the raw request JSON before `parse_dict`. It raises INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE when a field is spelled both ways and recurses into nested message values and lists.
Constraints: map entries and google.protobuf well-known types are skipped because their keys are caller-chosen. A single spelling of either form is accepted. Every request-body `parse_dict` call in handlers.py must run the check too; mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_workspace_request_message is a separate parser and was given the same call.
Applies: every proto-backed endpoint that parses its body in mlflow/server/handlers.py.
applies: Any request-body protobuf parser in mlflow/server/handlers.py; does not cover Flask routes that read request.json directly.
says: Updating an AI gateway secret unexpectedly modifies a completely different secret.
Users with read permissions on one gateway credential can overwrite unauthorized secrets.
Saving gateway secret changes applies settings to the wrong credential identifier.
Prevent privilege escalation where credential update requests execute against an unintended gateway secret.
Gateway credential edits should fail when requests include ambiguous conflicting credential field names.
search: Protobuf request parsers in mlflow/server/handlers.py must call _reject_conflicting_field_aliases on raw request JSON before parse_dict to reject bodies spelling any field in both snake_case and camelCase with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE. The check recurses into nested messages and lists, permits a single spelling of either form, skips map entries and google.protobuf well-known types, and applies to every proto-backed body parser including _get_request_message and _get_workspace_request_message. It does not cover Flask routes that read request.json directly.
